name: Samuel
summary: The last judge of Israel, born after his mother Hannah's prayer at Shiloh, dedicated to the LORD from childhood, and raised up as a prophet who anoints both Saul and David as king. Samuel confronts both kings' failures, leads Israel to victory at Mizpah, and delivers the LORD's verdicts throughout the book until his death near its end.

name: Saul
summary: Israel's first king, a tall Benjamite chosen by lot and anointed by Samuel, whose early military success against the Ammonites gives way to impatience, disobedience, and a growing jealousy of David that consumes the rest of his reign. Rejected by the LORD after sparing Agag, tormented by an evil spirit, and hunted by his own paranoia, Saul finally dies by his own sword after being mortally wounded at Mount Gilboa.

name: David
summary: The youngest son of Jesse, a shepherd from Bethlehem secretly anointed by Samuel to replace Saul, who becomes famous for killing the giant Goliath and rises quickly in Saul's court before Saul's jealousy forces him into years as a fugitive. Twice sparing Saul's life in the wilderness rather than raise a hand against the LORD's anointed, David survives to become the next king of Israel after Saul's death.

name: Eli
summary: The high priest and judge at Shiloh who raises Samuel but fails to restrain his own corrupt sons, and whose family line is judged by the LORD.

name: Hannah
summary: Elkanah's beloved but childless wife whose prayer at Shiloh is answered with the birth of Samuel, whom she dedicates to the LORD's service.

name: Elkanah
summary: Samuel's father, a Levite from the hill country of Ephraim who worships yearly at Shiloh with his two wives, Hannah and Peninnah.

name: Jonathan
summary: Saul's son and heir, a bold warrior whose raid routs a Philistine garrison and who becomes David's closest friend, bound to him by a lifelong covenant.

name: Goliath
summary: The giant Philistine champion from Gath who challenges Israel to single combat for forty days before David kills him with a sling and stone.

name: Abigail
summary: Nabal's wise wife who prevents David from taking bloody revenge on her household and later becomes David's wife after Nabal's death.

name: Nabal
summary: A wealthy but harsh sheep owner in Carmel who insults David's messengers and dies soon after his wife Abigail averts David's revenge.

name: Doeg
summary: Saul's chief herdsman, an Edomite who reports Ahimelech's help to David and then personally kills the priests of Nob at Saul's command.

name: Ahimelech
summary: The priest at Nob who gives David consecrated bread and Goliath's sword, an act of kindness for which Saul later has him and his fellow priests killed.

name: Achish
summary: The Philistine king of Gath who twice hosts David, first fooled by his feigned madness and later giving him the town of Ziklag to live in.

name: Michal
summary: Saul's younger daughter, given to David as a wife, who saves his life by helping him escape through a window before Saul later gives her to another man.

name: Abner
summary: Saul's cousin and the commander of his army, who remains loyal to Saul's family and is confronted by David for failing to guard the sleeping king.

name: Agag
summary: The Amalekite king whom Saul spares against the LORD's command, until Samuel kills him himself.

name: The Medium of Endor
summary: A medium living at Endor whom Saul consults in disguise the night before his final battle, and who brings up the spirit of Samuel at his request.

name: Hophni
summary: One of Eli's two priestly sons, condemned along with his brother for abusing his position at the tabernacle, who dies fighting alongside the ark of the covenant.

name: Phinehas
summary: The other of Eli's two priestly sons, condemned for the same abuses as his brother Hophni, who also dies in the battle where the ark is captured.

name: Nahash
summary: The Ammonite king who besieges Jabesh-gilead and threatens to gouge out the eyes of its people before Saul defeats him.

name: Abiathar
summary: Ahimelech's son and the lone priest of Nob to escape Saul's massacre, who joins David as his priest and carries the ephod for him.

name: Jesse
summary: A Bethlehemite and the father of David and his older brothers, at whose home Samuel comes to anoint the next king of Israel.

name: Abishai
summary: One of David's loyal men who accompanies him into Saul's camp at night and urges him to kill the sleeping king.

name: The Elders of Israel
summary: The elders of Israel who come to Samuel at Ramah demanding that he appoint a king to rule over them like the other nations.

name: God
summary: The LORD, the God of Israel, who raises up and removes kings, answers prayer, and speaks through Samuel and the prophets throughout the book.
